name: Dusty salmon
lede: Dusty salmon renders Tokiha-iro (鴇羽色), a traditional Japanese name meaning "ibis wing color", after the pale pink flight feathers of the crested ibis.

sections.title: Named for a bird's feather
sections.body:
Our color library gives the source as 鴇羽色 (Tokiha-iro), "ibis wing color": toki is the Japanese crested ibis, a bird known for its soft pink flight feathers, and ha is feather or wing [1]. No first-recorded date survives in our sources, so when the name entered use is undocumented here [1]. The library separately records Peachy Pink as a modern, 2010 xkcd crowd-survey name for a near-duplicate shade, at a color distance of 3.2, not a distinct historical name of its own [1].

The nearest named color in our graph is [[mona-lisa]], at a color distance (ΔE2000) of 2.6, almost the same shade; [[peachy-pink]] sits the same distance away, and [[salmon]] itself is 3.9 away and reads more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale pink in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, among the rarest matches we have recorded [3]. Both appearances are small highlight passages, in Correggio's *Salvator Mundi* (1515) and a Louis Gustave Ricard self-portrait (1853) [3]. With so few hits, this is closer to an absence than a trend; the figures remain a computed color match on aged, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [3].
